items.title: In-context learning
items.summary: In-context learning is a language model's ability to pick up a task from examples or instructions in its prompt, with no retraining. How it works and fails.

items.title: Imitation learning
items.summary: Imitation learning trains an AI system to act by copying recorded examples of experts doing a task, the method behind self-driving, robot and chatbot training.

items.title: Supervised fine-tuning
items.summary: Supervised fine-tuning trains a pretrained model on labelled prompt-and-answer pairs so it follows instructions, the first post-training step behind chatbots.

items.title: Least-privilege access
items.summary: Least-privilege access limits each user, program or AI agent to the minimum permissions a task needs, a 1975 principle now applied to ad accounts and AI agents.

items.title: Approval threshold
items.summary: An approval threshold is the limit above which a software agent or employee must get human sign-off before acting, such as a spend cap on an ad buying agent.

items.title: Guardrails
items.summary: Guardrails are controls placed around an AI model or agent that check inputs, outputs and actions against set rules, and block what falls outside that policy.

items.title: Audit trail
items.summary: An audit trail is a time-ordered record of who did what in a system and when, kept so that actions can be reconstructed, verified and attributed after the fact.

items.title: Data controller
items.summary: A data controller is the organisation that decides why and how personal data is processed, carrying primary legal responsibility under GDPR for ad data flows.

items.title: Data processor
items.summary: A data processor handles personal data on behalf of a controller and under its instructions, bound by a GDPR Article 28 contract on use, security and deletion.

items.title: Profiling
items.summary: Profiling: automated processing of personal data to evaluate or predict a person's traits, interests or behaviour, the legal core of rules on targeted ads.

items.title: Contextual integrity
items.summary: Contextual integrity: Helen Nissenbaum's theory that privacy means information flowing by the norms of its context, now used to test AI agents and ad targeting.

items.title: Data (Use and Access) Act
items.summary: Data (Use and Access) Act is the UK's 2025 law that rewrites parts of UK GDPR and PECR, adds cookie consent exemptions and turns the ICO into a commission.

items.title: DRCF
items.summary: DRCF: the Digital Regulation Cooperation Forum, where the UK's CMA, ICO, Ofcom and FCA coordinate digital rules on AI agents, data, competition and safety.

items.title: DPIA
items.summary: A DPIA, or data protection impact assessment, is the written risk review GDPR Article 35 demands before processing likely to put people's rights at high risk.

items.title: Data protection by design and by default
items.summary: Data protection by design and by default is the GDPR Article 25 duty to build data safeguards into processing and keep defaults to the data each purpose needs.

items.title: Purpose limitation
items.summary: Purpose limitation: the GDPR rule that personal data collected for a stated purpose may not be reused for an incompatible one, a test set out in Article 6(4).

items.title: Human in the loop
items.summary: Human in the loop is a design in which an automated system must stop and wait for a person to approve, correct or reject its output before an action goes live.
